domain: Gangwon east coast (Seoraksan, Sokcho, Yangyang, Gangneung, Odaesan) and the Donghae coast rail
research_note: The session's shared WebSearch budget ran out partway through this research, and most hotel and attraction sites refused WebFetch (403, bot checks, refused connections). These items were verified from 2026 sources: the 2026 foliage forecast, the 2026 Seorak cable car fare and booking rules, the Osaek cable car status (July 2026), Sokcho's foliage-season traffic plan (Oct 2026), Donghae line timetables (data dated Oct 7 2026) and the KTX-Eum launch (Dec 30 2025), plus Seongyojang fees and Wikipedia coordinates. Everything else, including every lodging price, comes from prior knowledge of 2024-25 rates and is marked confidence low or medium. Re-check those prices on Naver Hotels, Agoda or Yanolja before booking. Coordinates not from Wikipedia are approximate (within about 300 m).

places.name: Seoraksan National Park – Seorak-dong (Sogongwon) entrance & Sinheungsa Temple
places.summary: This is the main eastern gateway to Seoraksan. A flat 1 km walk passes the 14.6 m bronze Unification Buddha (통일대불) and reaches Sinheungsa, the head temple of the Jogye Order's 3rd parish. Every classic low-level hike starts here: Ulsanbawi, Biseondae, Gwongeumseong cable car, and Yukdam/Biryong falls.
places.why: This is Korea's answer to a Kamakura temple set against mountains, with a giant outdoor Buddha. The difference is the granite peaks that rise right behind it.
places.autumn_note: The 2026 forecast puts first foliage at Seoraksan on Oct 3 and the peak at about Oct 16-25. Low valleys around Sogongwon usually peak in the last week of October, which is exactly when these travelers arrive.
places.time_needed: 1-1.5 h for the temple and Buddha; a full day with hikes
places.hours: The park is open all day. Trail entry has time limits: for ridge trails the gates generally close in the early afternoon, and you must be off the trail by sunset.
places.closed: Open in October. High-altitude trails such as Gongnyong ridge and routes up to Daecheongbong close for wildfire season from about Nov 15 to Dec 15 (2025 pattern), so they are unaffected in October. The Sogongwon-area trails (Biseondae, Ulsanbawi, Gwongeumseong) stay open even during that closure.
places.cost_note: Park entry is free, and the Sinheungsa cultural-heritage fee was abolished in May 2023. Sogongwon parking costs 6,000 KRW/day for a car (2026 source).
places.tips: Sokcho runs a special foliage traffic plan from Oct 3 to Nov 8, 2026. Cars are held back in stages, overflow goes to free parking lots B and C, and free shuttles run from there. Arrive before 07:00 on weekends, or take city bus 7/7-1. Avoid Sat Oct 17, Sun Oct 18 and Sat Oct 24 if you can, or go at dawn.

places.name: Seorak Cable Car to Gwongeumseong Fortress
places.summary: A 5-minute gondola ride climbs to about 700 m. From the top it is a 10-15 minute rocky scramble to the Gwongeumseong fortress ruins, which look out over Ulsanbawi, the Seorak peaks and the East Sea.
places.why: This is the easiest way to get a big Seorak view without a long hike.
places.autumn_note: This is peak demand season. On October weekends the wait after buying a ticket can be 1-2+ hours, because your ticket carries an assigned boarding time.
places.hours: Hours change with season and weather and are posted daily at the top of sorakcablecar.co.kr. Typical October hours are about 08:30-17:30, with ticket sales stopping earlier (not confirmed). If you take the last car up, you only get about 20 minutes at the top.
places.closed: Runs daily but stops in strong wind.
places.cost_note: 2026 round-trip fares: adult 16,000, child 12,000. Seniors pay 14,000 except during peak periods (Jul 18-Aug 23 and Sep 19-Nov 15). Only round-trip tickets are sold.
places.booking: Tickets are sold on-site only, for the same day; there is no advance booking. Buy them first thing, then hike Biseondae or visit Sinheungsa while you wait for your boarding time.
places.tips: Get there before about 08:30, or buy tickets on arrival and do Biseondae while you wait. Cabins have no heating, and the top is windy and cold in late October. The real-time wait shows on Sokcho's electronic signboards.

places.name: Ulsanbawi Rock hike
places.summary: This is a 3.8 km one-way hike from Sogongwon past Heundeulbawi (the rocking stone) and Gyejoam hermitage. It finishes with about 800+ steel stairs up the 873 m granite massif, which has a 360° view of Seorak and Sokcho down to the sea.
places.why: This is the signature Seorak summit view and a satisfying half-day hike for fit adults.
places.autumn_note: Foliage is best on the approach (about Oct 15-25). Above the stairs it is mostly bare granite.
places.hours: Trail entry closes in the early afternoon in autumn (check the gate sign). Start by about 09:00.
places.cost_note: Free.
places.tips: The stairs are steep and exposed and get very windy. Bring gloves and a layer.

places.name: Biseondae Rock & Geumganggul Cave
places.summary: A gentle 3 km valley walk from Sogongwon leads to Biseondae, where broad granite slabs sit in a clear stream under the Jangguseong cliffs. A steep extra 0.6 km climbs to Geumganggul, a cliffside cave hermitage.
places.why: This is the best 'easy and gorgeous' foliage walk in Seorak. It feels like a mountain version of a temple-town stroll.
places.autumn_note: The valley peak usually falls in the last 10 days of October. It is crowded on weekends.
places.time_needed: 2-2.5 h round trip; +1 h for Geumganggul
places.cost_note: Free.
places.tips: It pairs well with the cable car: buy cable car tickets first, then walk Biseondae while you wait.

places.name: Heullimgol → Yongso Falls → Juongol valley (Osaek / Nam-Seorak)
places.summary: This is a classic downhill foliage gorge walk. You start at the Heullimgol trailhead on Route 44 below Hangyeryeong pass, go over Deungseondae, past Yongso Falls, and down the Juongol gorge to Osaek hot-spring village (about 6 km, 3-4 h). A shorter option is Osaek to Yongso Falls and back on the flat Juongol trail (about 3 km each way, 2-2.5 h).
places.why: This is the most spectacular red-maple gorge on the east coast. The finish at Osaek mineral spring and hot springs echoes an Izu onsen-valley walk.
places.autumn_note: Juongol is one of Korea's most famous foliage spots, peaking about Oct 18-28. Route 44 and Osaek are badly jammed on October weekends.
places.time_needed: 3-4 h one way (Heullimgol), 2-2.5 h (Juongol out and back)
places.hours: Heullimgol works on reservations with timed entry. Juongol from Osaek is open during the day without a reservation.
places.closed: The spring (about Mar 2 to May 15) and autumn (about Nov 15 to Dec 15) wildfire closures do not apply in late October.
places.cost_note: Free.
places.booking: Heullimgol needs advance reservation in the KNPS system (reservation.knps.or.kr), capped at 5,000 people a day with time slots. Foreigners can usually book through the English KNPS reservation site. Juongol from Osaek needs no reservation.
places.tips: Heullimgol has had rockfall closures before (closed 2015-2022, reopened Sep 6, 2022). Check KNPS notices. Without a car, take an intercity bus toward Hangyeryeong or Osaek from Yangyang or Sokcho, or use a taxi.

places.name: Naksansa Temple (Uisangdae pavilion, Hongnyeonam hermitage)
places.summary: This seaside temple was founded in 671 by the monk Uisang. It has a 16 m white Haesu Gwaneum statue facing the sea, the Uisangdae pavilion on a pine-clad cliff (Scenic Site), and the Hongnyeonam hermitage built over a sea cave, with a floor hole through which you can see waves. It was rebuilt after the 2005 forest fire.
places.why: This is the closest Korean match to Kamakura's seaside temples and Hase-dera's sea views. It is the top pick for these travelers. Uisangdae at sunrise is iconic.
places.autumn_note: Mild late-October weather and clear sea air. Sunrise is about 06:40.
places.hours: Roughly 06:00-18:00 (open from about 04:00 for sunrise worshippers); not confirmed for 2026.
places.cost_note: Admission has been free since the May 2023 abolition of the heritage fee. Parking is about 4,000 KRW.
places.booking: None. Naksansa also runs a templestay program.
places.tips: Combine with Naksan beach and Yangyang. Bus 9 or 9-1 from Sokcho takes about 30 min.

places.name: Hyuhyuam seaside temple (likely the 'Hyujeonsa' in the brief)
places.summary: A small modern temple on flat sea rocks, with a natural 'reclining Buddha' rock formation, a big Jibong Gwaneum statue, and fish-feeding from the rocks.
places.why: A rocky-coast temple stop that could be in Kamakura or Enoshima, and easy to combine with Jukdo and Surfyy beaches.
places.cost_note: Free.
places.tips: It is 10 minutes by car from Jukdo and Ingu beaches. Bus service is sparse, so a taxi from Hajodae, Ingu or Jumunjin works better.

places.name: Hajodae pavilion & lighthouse
places.summary: A hexagonal Joseon-era pavilion and a white lighthouse on pine-covered sea cliffs, with a lone pine growing out of a rock.
places.why: A quiet 30-minute coastal stop with a Kamakura or Enoshima cliff feel.
places.cost_note: Free.
places.tips: Pair it with Hyuhyuam and Jukdo.

places.name: Jukdo Beach & Surfyy Beach – Yangyang surf coast
places.summary: Korea's surf capital. Jukdo and Ingu have surf shops, cafés, bars and a laid-back 'Korean Shonan' vibe. Surfyy Beach (Hajodae) is a private surf beach with a beach-bar look.
places.why: This is the Shonan or Enoshima side of Kamakura: young, beachy and full of good cafés. Lessons are a fun active day.
places.autumn_note: Late October water is about 17-19 °C, so a full wetsuit is supplied. Autumn swells are good. Beach-bar activity winds down after September.
places.hours: Surf shops run lessons at about 10:00 and 14:00. Surfyy operating hours shrink in the off-season.
places.closed: Some Surfyy facilities cut back after mid-October (not confirmed for 2026).
places.cost_note: A 2-hour group surf lesson with board and wetsuit typically costs 50,000-70,000 KRW (2024-25 pricing, not confirmed for 2026).
places.booking: Book through Naver booking, Instagram or KakaoTalk with the shops. Some shops have English-speaking instructors.
places.tips: Bus 9-1 runs along the coast, but a taxi is easier. Yangyang Station (on the Donghae line? No: there is no rail; see transport) is not a rail station. Reach it by bus from Sokcho or Gangneung, or from Seoul's Yangyang buses.

places.name: Abai Village & Gaetbae hand-pulled ferry
places.summary: A sandbar village founded by North Korean refugees from Hamgyeong Province during the Korean War. You cross the harbor channel on the Gaetbae, a barge that passengers pull along a cable themselves. It is known for Abai sundae (stuffed squid and sausage) and Hamheung naengmyeon.
places.why: This is the 'little charming quirk' moment, like the Enoden: a tiny human-powered ferry ride, plus refugee history and fishing-port food.
places.cost_note: The Gaetbae fare has historically been 500 KRW per crossing in cash (could be 1,000 by 2026; not verified).
places.tips: Walk on to Jungang market (10 min) and the Seorak Bridge.

places.name: Sokcho Tourist & Fishery Market (Jungang Market)
places.summary: A big covered market famous for dakgangjeong (sweet-spicy fried chicken boxes, such as Manseok), squid sundae, hotteok, and a basement live-seafood floor where you choose fish and get sashimi cut to order.
places.why: This is the energy of Tsukiji's outer market, Korean style. It is the best cheap food stop in Sokcho.
places.autumn_note: Autumn means red snow crab (홍게), saury and fat flatfish.
places.hours: About 08:00-21:00 (stalls vary). The basement fish floor is open late.
places.closed: Some stalls close on the 1st and 3rd Monday.
places.cost_note: Food only.
places.tips: Buy dakgangjeong to eat later; the boxes travel well. Lines at Manseok move fast.

places.name: Sokcho Beach & Sokcho Eye Ferris wheel
places.summary: A 65 m beachfront Ferris wheel lit in neon at night, overlooking Sokcho beach, the harbor and the Seorak range.
places.why: A small dose of the neon-city mood, by the sea.
places.autumn_note: Clear October evenings are good for views of Seorak at sunset.
places.cost_note: About 15,000 KRW adult for a standard cabin (2024-25 figure, not verified for 2026). The official site refused fetches.
places.tips: Go just after dark.

places.name: Yeonggeumjeong pavilion & Sokcho Lighthouse Observatory
places.summary: A pavilion on a bridge over sea rocks, the classic Sokcho sunrise spot, next to a lighthouse with a free observatory deck that looks at Seorak and the coast. Dongmyeong port's red-crab restaurants are next door.
places.why: Coastal-temple-town scenery without the crowds.
places.hours: The pavilion is always open. The lighthouse observatory is open about 06:00-18:00.
places.cost_note: Free.
places.tips: Go at sunrise if you stay in Sokcho.

places.name: Daepo Port
places.summary: A fishing harbor with a raw-fish center and stalls of fried shrimp and squid. It is next to Oeongchi seaside trail and Lotte Resort Sokcho.
places.why: A casual seafood-port grazing stop, and a contrast to omakase.
places.cost_note: Food only.
places.tips: The Oeongchi Bada Hyanggi-ro trail (about 1.7 km) links Daepo to Sokcho beach along the rocks. It is a great short walk.

places.name: Cheongchoho Lake park & Expo Tower
places.summary: A lagoon in central Sokcho with a lakeside promenade and the Expo Tower viewpoint, which looks across to Seorak.
places.why: An easy evening walk and a city-plus-mountain view.
places.cost_note: Free (tower lift believed free).

places.name: Anmok Beach Coffee Street
places.summary: A beachfront row of multi-storey cafés with sea-view rooftops. Gangneung is Korea's 'coffee city' (Terarosa, Bohemian Bak Yi-chu, and others).
places.why: It is like a Shonan seaside café strip. It's a relaxed coastal stroll.
places.autumn_note: The Gangneung Coffee Festival is historically held in October (2026 dates not verified).
places.cost_note: Coffee costs 5,000-9,000 KRW.
places.tips: It is 15 minutes by taxi from Gangneung Station (about 10,000-12,000 KRW).

places.name: Gyeongpo Lake, Gyeongpodae & Gyeongpo Beach
places.summary: A lagoon with a 4.3 km cycling and walking loop, the Joseon-era Gyeongpodae pavilion (a National Treasure since 2019) on a hill, and Gyeongpo beach backed by pines. You can rent bikes around the lake.
places.why: A gentle lakeside-plus-sea day, with Ojukheon and Seongyojang nearby.
places.autumn_note: The cherry trees around the lake turn color in late October, and reeds and silver grass line the shore.
places.hours: Always open. Gyeongpodae pavilion is open about 09:00-18:00.
places.cost_note: Free. Bike rental is about 5,000-10,000 KRW per hour, or more for tandems.
places.tips: Chodang tofu village is 1 km south.

places.name: Ojukheon (birthplace of Yulgok and Shin Saimdang)
places.summary: A late-15th-century scholar-gentry house surrounded by black bamboo. It is one of Korea's oldest residential buildings (Treasure) and appears on the 5,000 and 50,000 won notes. The site includes the Gangneung city museum.
places.why: Quiet Joseon heritage with gardens, like Kamakura's old residences.
places.autumn_note: Persimmons and ginkgo turn color in late October.
places.closed: Believed to be open year-round (some sources list Jan 1, Seollal and Chuseok closures).
places.cost_note: Adult 3,000 KRW (2024-25 figure).
places.tips: Combine with Seongyojang (1 km) and Gyeongpo.

places.name: Seongyojang House
places.summary: A 300-year-old aristocratic estate with 102 kan of buildings, the Hwallaejeong lotus-pond pavilion, and pine woods. It also offers hanok stays.
places.why: This is the most ryokan-like traditional lodging option on this coast (see lodging).
places.autumn_note: The pine-and-maple backdrop and the pond pavilion are lovely in autumn.
places.cost_note: Adult 5,000 KRW, youth 3,000, child 2,000.

places.name: Chodang Sundubu (soft tofu) Village
places.summary: A cluster of restaurants making tofu with seawater brine (a 400-year tradition). Famous for jjamppong-sundubu (Donghwa Gaden) and plain white sundubu (Chodang Halmeoni).
places.why: This is the Gangneung signature meal, much as yudofu is in Kamakura and Kyoto.
places.cost_note: Meals are 11,000-16,000 KRW. Tofu-gelato cafés are nearby.
places.booking: None. Donghwa Gaden uses a queue tablet.
places.tips: Go before 11:00 to avoid the queues.

places.name: Jumunjin Port fish market & BTS bus stop (Hyangho Beach)
places.summary: A lively fishing port with a fish market, and nearby the bus-stop set from BTS's 'You Never Walk Alone' album at Hyangho beach (about 37.9218, 128.7980). The Goblin (Dokkaebi) drama breakwater is close too.
places.why: A fun pop-culture photo stop, plus a seafood market.
places.cost_note: The bus stop is free (there may be a small photo-zone fee).
places.tips: It is on the way between Gangneung and Yangyang/Sokcho. Bus 300 or the intercity bus stops at Jumunjin.

places.name: Jeongdongjin & Jeongdong Simgok Badabuchae-gil coastal trail
places.summary: Jeongdongjin station sits right on the beach and is famous as one of the closest stations to the sea in the world. The 2.9 km Badabuchae-gil boardwalk runs along the 23-million-year-old coastal terrace cliffs between Jeongdongjin and Simgok. There is also the Sun Cruise ship-shaped hotel on the cliff.
places.why: This is the 'little coastal train' moment, like the Enoden. The KTX and local trains stop right on the beach.
places.hours: The Badabuchae-gil boardwalk is typically open about 09:00-17:30 in October.
places.closed: It closes in high waves or wind and has had rockfall closures. Check the same day.
places.cost_note: Badabuchae-gil was about 5,000 KRW, partly refunded as a local voucher (2024-25 figure, not verified for 2026).
places.tips: Some Gangneung-line KTX trains run on to Jeongdongjin (about 2 h from Seoul). The local Donghae-line trains (Nuriro or ITX-Maeum) from Gangneung take about 15 min.

places.name: Haslla Art World
places.summary: A clifftop sculpture park, museum and art hotel looking over the sea, including a Pinocchio and marionette museum.
places.why: An art-and-sea stop with a Hakone Open-Air Museum vibe.
places.cost_note: About 12,000-18,000 KRW adult depending on the package (not verified). The official site refused fetches.
places.tips: It pairs with Jeongdongjin and Badabuchae-gil.

places.name: Woljeongsa Temple & Fir Forest Path (Odaesan)
places.summary: A 1 km path through about 1,700 fir trees, some 300+ years old, leads to Woljeongsa. The temple was founded in 643, and its 15 m octagonal nine-storey pagoda is a National Treasure.
places.why: This is the closest match to a Japanese cedar-avenue temple approach (like Hakone's old road or Nikko). It is serene and green, with maples along the stream.
places.autumn_note: The 2026 forecast puts Odaesan's peak at about Oct 16-25, with the valley maples along the stream turning in the second half of October.
places.hours: The temple is open about 05:00-21:00. Museum about 09:00-18:00 (closed Tuesdays).
places.cost_note: Free since May 2023. Parking is about 4,000-5,000 KRW.
places.booking: None. Woljeongsa templestay can be booked via eng.templestay.com.
places.tips: Take the KTX to Jinbu (Odaesan) station (about 1h20 from Seoul, 20 min from Gangneung), then a local bus or taxi (about 20 min, roughly 20,000 KRW).

places.name: Seonjae-gil trail (Woljeongsa → Sangwonsa)
places.summary: A 9 km gently rising streamside forest trail used by monks, from Woljeongsa to Sangwonsa. Sangwonsa holds Korea's oldest bronze bell (725 AD, a National Treasure). Bus 223 runs on the road alongside, so you can walk one way and ride back.
places.why: One of Korea's best foliage walks: easy, quiet and spiritual.
places.autumn_note: The peak along the stream is about Oct 18-28. Weekends are busy.
places.closed: Trails can close temporarily in heavy rain.
places.cost_note: Free. The bus between the two temples is about 1,000-2,000 KRW.
places.tips: Ride the bus up to Sangwonsa and walk downhill to Woljeongsa.

places.name: Seorak Waterpia (hot-spring water park, Hanwha Resort Seorak)
places.summary: A hot-spring water park and spa fed by Seorak's alkaline hot-spring water. It has outdoor hot-spring pools with Ulsanbawi views, plus a sauna (bathhouse).
places.why: This is the nearest thing to an onsen soak after hiking, though it is a water park rather than a ryokan. Bring swimsuits.
places.autumn_note: Outdoor hot pools on cool October evenings are lovely.
places.hours: About 09:00-18:00 (spa and sauna run longer); not confirmed for 2026.
places.cost_note: About 40,000-55,000 KRW adult in the shoulder season (2024-25 figure, not verified). Hanwha Sorano guests get discounts. The sauna-only ticket is much cheaper (about 10,000-15,000).
places.booking: On-site or through the Hanwha app or Naver.
places.tips: Swimsuit required. Korean bathhouse rules apply in the sauna section: nude, single-sex. Tattoos are generally tolerated.

places.name: Cheoksan Hot Spring (Cheoksan Oncheon Hyuyangchon)
places.summary: A natural alkaline hot spring at about 53 °C. It has a public bathhouse with an outdoor rotenburo-style bath set in pines, plus simple lodging rooms.
places.why: The most onsen-like public bath in the Sokcho and Seorak area: single-sex, nude, with an outdoor bath, as in Japan.
places.autumn_note: The outdoor bath under autumn foliage is great after a Seorak hike.
places.cost_note: Adult about 9,000-10,000 KRW (2024-25 figure, not verified).
places.tips: It is 10 minutes by taxi from Seorak-dong. Pair it with a Seorak hike day.

places.name: ARTE Museum Gangneung (immersive media art)
places.summary: An immersive digital-art exhibition in the teamLab mold, near Gyeongpo.
places.why: A rainy-day option with Tokyo teamLab vibes.
places.cost_note: About 17,000 KRW adult (not verified).

lodging.name: Seongyojang Hanok Stay
lodging.room_for_3: Ondol floor rooms with yo bedding; larger rooms or annexes sleep 3-4.
lodging.price_note: Estimate from 2024-25 listings for a 3-person room; not verified for 2026. The official site returned 403.
lodging.highlights: Sleep inside a 300-year-old noble estate. The grounds are quiet after the day visitors leave. This is the most ryokan-like option.
lodging.drawbacks: Shared or basic bathrooms in some rooms, no hot spring, floor sleeping, and limited rooms that sell out on weekends.
lodging.booking: Official site knsgj.net (by phone or in Korean), or possibly Naver or Yanolja.

lodging.name: Hanwha Resort Seorak Sorano
lodging.room_for_3: Condo-style family suites with a bedroom plus an ondol room and kitchenette fit 3-4 adults.
lodging.price_note: Estimate for a family suite in late October: about 180-250k on weekdays and 300-400k+ on Saturdays during foliage season. Not verified for 2026.
lodging.highlights: Next to Seorak Waterpia's hot-spring pools (with a guest discount), 10 minutes from Seorak-dong, and Ulsanbawi views.
lodging.drawbacks: The condo rooms are dated, and you need a car or taxi to get around.
lodging.booking: Hanwha Resort site or app (Korean), Agoda, Booking.com, Naver.

lodging.name: Lotte Resort Sokcho
lodging.room_for_3: Family twin or suite rooms (double plus single), or a residence suite with an ondol room.
lodging.price_note: Estimate for a 3-person family room: about 280-400k on weekdays and 450-600k on weekends. Not verified for 2026.
lodging.highlights: An outdoor infinity pool over the sea (heated), sea views, and the Oeongchi coastal trail and Daepo port on foot.
lodging.drawbacks: Expensive, and 20-30 minutes by car from Seorak.

lodging.name: Kensington Hotel Seorak (formerly Kensington Stars)
lodging.area: Seorak-dong, inside the park entrance zone
lodging.room_for_3: Family or triple rooms; ondol rooms available.
lodging.price_note: Estimate: about 200-280k on weekdays and up to 450k on peak October weekends. Not verified for 2026.
lodging.highlights: A walk to the Sogongwon trailheads and the cable car, so you beat the weekend traffic jams. British-themed interiors and a double-decker bus out front.
lodging.drawbacks: Dated, quiet at night, and far from Sokcho city's food scene.

lodging.name: Sono Calm/Sono Belle Delpino
lodging.room_for_3: Family or suite rooms (bed plus ondol); the condo units have kitchens.
lodging.highlights: Head-on views of Ulsanbawi and an outdoor infinity pool (Ocean Play) looking at the rock face.
lodging.drawbacks: Car needed, and far from the beach and city.

lodging.name: Sono/Sol Beach Yangyang
lodging.room_for_3: Family suites (condo rooms with bedroom plus living-room bed) sleep 3-4.
lodging.highlights: Santorini-style beachfront, a walk to Naksan beach, 10 minutes to Naksansa for sunrise, and a sauna and water park.
lodging.drawbacks: Kitschy, and a car or taxi is needed.

lodging.name: Seamarq Hotel Gangneung
lodging.room_for_3: Deluxe rooms take 3 with an extra bed (charged), or book a suite. The Hotel Hyundai annex (Hanok? No: the low-rise wing) has family rooms.
lodging.price_note: Estimate: Gangneung's most expensive hotel. Ocean-view rooms run about 400-550k on weekdays and up to 800k on weekends, plus about 50-80k for an extra bed. Not verified.
lodging.highlights: Richard Meier design, an infinity pool on the sea, and a sauna. The most luxurious stay on the coast.
lodging.drawbacks: Expensive, and too costly for a 3-person under-$1,000 budget if used for more than one night.

lodging.name: Skybay Hotel Gyeongpo
lodging.room_for_3: Family or triple rooms, or residence rooms with kitchenettes.
lodging.highlights: A rooftop infinity pool over Gyeongpo beach and the lake, between the sea and the lake.
lodging.drawbacks: Big and busy, and the pool may need an extra fee.

lodging.name: St. John's Hotel Gangneung
lodging.room_for_3: Family twin (double plus single) rooms are common, and there are bunk-bed rooms.
lodging.price_note: Estimate, not verified. This is the best-value big hotel on the beach.
lodging.highlights: Beachfront with an outdoor pool and a walk to Gangmun beach and Chodang tofu village.

lodging.name: Woljeongsa Templestay (Odaesan)
lodging.room_for_3: Shared ondol rooms by gender. Three adults of mixed gender may be split.
lodging.price_note: About 70-90k per person per night including temple meals, so roughly 210-270k for 3 people. Based on typical 2024-25 rates; not verified.
lodging.highlights: The 4am chanting, monk-led tea, the fir-forest walk at dawn, and vegetarian temple food.
lodging.drawbacks: Very basic floor bedding, strict hours, and alcohol forbidden.

lodging.name: Osaek Greenyard Hotel (Osaek hot springs)
lodging.price_note: Estimate, not verified. The hotel's operating status for 2026 was not confirmed (the open question is whether its hot-spring and carbonated-spring baths are open).
lodging.highlights: Osaek carbonated mineral spring and hot springs at the bottom of the Juongol trail. The most Izu-like hot-spring village experience.
lodging.drawbacks: Status unverified, a dated property, and the village is jammed on foliage weekends.

food.name: Manseok Dakgangjeong
food.booking: Walk-in; takeaway boxes about 20,000-25,000 KRW for a medium box.
food.why: The single most famous Sokcho snack.

food.name: Abai Village sundae and Hamheung naengmyeon (e.g. Danchon Sikdang, Sinda Sinda)
food.type: North Korean refugee food: stuffed-squid sundae, cold noodles
food.why: This food is the heritage of the refugee village.

food.name: Bongpo Meoguri Jip
food.type: mulhoe (spicy cold raw-fish soup) and seafood bowls
food.booking: Walk-in, with a long lunch queue.
food.why: The Sokcho classic for fresh raw fish, a casual counterpoint to sushi omakase.

food.name: Red snow crab (hongge) restaurants at Dongmyeong port, or the Jungang market basement fish floor
food.type: steamed red snow crab, sashimi cut to order
food.booking: Walk-in. Prices are by weight, so ask first.
food.why: The closest experience to an omakase-style seafood splurge. Autumn is crab season.

food.name: Chilseong Shipyard (cafe in a 1952 wooden-boat shipyard)
food.why: A hip industrial-heritage café on the lake.

food.name: Terarosa Coffee factory (Gujeong)
food.why: Gangneung is Korea's coffee town, and this is the pilgrimage roastery.

food.name: Gangneung Jungang Market & Wolhwa Street (night market)
food.type: market: dakgangjeong, crab croquettes, mulhoe, hotteok
food.why: Lively evening grazing near Gangneung Station.

food.name: Odaesan mountain-vegetable set meals (Sanchae jeongsik) by Woljeongsa, e.g. Odaesan Sikdang / Bibong Sikdang
food.why: Healthy, seasonal food in the spirit of temple cuisine.

food.name: Yangyang pine mushroom (songi) dishes, e.g. songi hot pot or grilled songi with hanu beef
food.why: Korea's matsutake. The season runs through mid to late October, depending on rain. Prices vary hugely, and raw songi can cost 100,000+ KRW/kg.

transport.from: Seoul Station (KTX, many trains via Cheongnyangni)
transport.frequency: 14 trains a day Seoul Station to Gangneung (first 05:20, last 22:27), plus extra trains starting at Cheongnyangni
transport.booking: Korail website or Korail Talk app, letskorail.com in English. Seats open about a month ahead. Foreigners can book with an overseas card. Weekends in October sell out, so book now. Cheongnyangni departures are slightly cheaper.
transport.notes: Some trains run on to Jeongdongjin and Donghae. Jinbu (Odaesan) station is on this line for Woljeongsa.

transport.to: Busan Bujeon (via Donghae, Samcheok, Uljin, Yeongdeok, Pohang, Gyeongju, Taehwagang/Ulsan, Centum, Sinhaeundae)
transport.mode: KTX-Eum or ITX-Maeum on the Donghae line
transport.frequency: Gangneung to Bujeon (week of Oct 7 2026): ITX-Maeum 1822 at 05:46 (arr 10:49, 34,900); KTX-Eum 752 at 09:36 (arr 13:36), 754 at 14:56 (arr 18:50), 756 at 18:35 (arr 22:29), each 46,800. KTX-Eum has run since Dec 30, 2025, with 3 round trips (6 trips) a day.
transport.booking: Korail website or Korail Talk, up to 1 month ahead. The Korail Pass is valid.
transport.notes: Yes, you can ride the coast from Gangneung to Gyeongju and Busan in a single seat. The real sea views are mostly in the Gangneung-Jeongdongjin-Donghae-Samcheok section (the old Yeongdong line hugs the beach) and in glimpses around Uljin and Hupo. Much of the new Samcheok-Yeongdeok section runs through tunnels and inland, so it is not a scenic train the whole way. Sit on the left (east) side heading south.

transport.frequency: 3 a day, the same trains as Bujeon: 752 dep 09:36, 754 dep 14:56, 756 dep 18:35. Arrival in Gyeongju is about 2h45 later (estimated from Pohang arrivals at 12:04, 17:18 and 20:56, plus about 20 min). The reverse direction leaves Gyeongju at 08:56, 15:04 and 20:45.
transport.notes: The best 'coast ride' transfer to Gyeongju. Take the 09:36 to reach Gyeongju by about 12:20 with a full afternoon free.
The Nuriro is the cheap, slow option.

transport.mode: Train (Donghae line: ITX-Maeum, Nuriro or KTX-Eum) or bus 109/111/112
transport.duration: About 12-15 min by train, about 35 min by bus
transport.frequency: Several trains a day (see the Pohang list); buses about hourly
transport.booking: Korail, or walk on for the bus.
transport.notes: The beachside Jeongdongjin station is the 'little coastal train' moment.

transport.from: Seoul Express Bus Terminal (Gangnam) / Dong Seoul Terminal
transport.duration: About 2h10-2h40 on weekdays via the Seoul-Yangyang expressway. Allow 3.5-4+ h on October weekend mornings (outbound) and Sunday afternoons (inbound).
transport.booking: kobus.co.kr (express) or bustago.or.kr (intercity, from Dong Seoul). Foreign cards may fail, so use the T-money GO app or buy at the counter. Book the weekend return early.
transport.notes: Fare is approximately 21,000-30,000 KRW for standard or premium (2024-25 levels; not verified for 2026). Express buses go to the Sokcho Express Bus Terminal near Daepo and Sokcho beach. Intercity buses go to the Sokcho Intercity Terminal near Jungang market.

transport.mode: Airport limousine/intercity bus, or AREX plus KTX via Seoul Station
transport.duration: Bus about 3h30-4h. AREX (60 min) plus KTX (2h) is about 3.5h with transfers.
transport.frequency: Several direct buses a day to Gangneung and fewer to Sokcho (not verified)
transport.booking: Counter at the airport, or the T-money GO app.
transport.notes: Fare approximately 30,000-40,000 KRW (not verified). Landing at 05:15 means the first buses could have them in Gangneung by about 10:00. Still, most itineraries start in Seoul.

transport.booking: Walk-on at the Gangneung Intercity Bus Terminal, or bustago.
transport.notes: Fare approximately 7,000-8,000 KRW (not verified). Get off at Yangyang to reach Naksansa or the surf beaches. There is no rail between Gangneung and Sokcho: the Donghae Bukbu line (Gangneung to Jejin) is under construction, targeted around 2027-28.

transport.from: Sokcho city (Intercity Terminal, Jungang market, Daepo)
transport.duration: About 30-45 min, longer in foliage traffic
transport.notes: On October weekends the bus is stuck in the same queue as cars. Leave by 07:00. Free shuttles run from lots B and C during the Oct 3-Nov 8 traffic-control period.

transport.mode: Rural bus (Jinbu terminal to Woljeongsa to Sangwonsa) or taxi
transport.duration: About 20-30 min to Woljeongsa, plus 20 min to Sangwonsa
transport.notes: A taxi is about 20,000 KRW to Woljeongsa. Jinbu is about 20 min from Gangneung by KTX.

transport.booking: The Kakao T app works with foreign phone numbers and cards in 2025-26, or hail one.
transport.notes: Sample fares: Sokcho city to Seorak Sogongwon about 15,000-20,000 KRW per car; Gangneung Station to Anmok about 10,000-12,000; Sokcho to Naksansa about 20,000.

transport.booking: Lotte Rent-a-car or SK Rent-a-car at Gangneung Station or Sokcho. About 70,000-120,000 KRW a day for a compact or midsize car, plus insurance (not verified).
transport.notes: Americans need an International Driving Permit (1949 Geneva type, from AAA) plus their US license and passport. A car makes Heullimgol/Osaek, Hyuhyuam and Odaesan much easier. However, October weekend jams on Route 44 (Hangyeryeong), into Seorak-dong and on the Seoul-Yangyang expressway are severe.
Not open. It is under construction, with opening targeted around 2027-28 (Seoul to Sokcho in about 1h40 when finished). Use the bus.

events.name: Seoraksan autumn foliage peak (2026 forecast)
events.dates: First color Oct 3, peak about Oct 16-25 (Seorak summit area earlier, low valleys such as Biseondae, Juongol and Sogongwon around Oct 20-30). Odaesan peaks about Oct 16-25.
events.notes: Foliage is forecast to arrive later than average because September and October 2026 are expected to be warmer than normal. The trip window of Oct 17-25 sits right in the peak.

events.name: Sokcho foliage-season special traffic management
events.notes: Staged car restrictions into Sogongwon, free lots B and C with shuttles, and electronic signs showing parking and cable-car waits.

events.name: Gangneung Coffee Festival
events.dates: Historically held in October; 2026 dates not verified
events.notes: Check coffeefestival.net or Gangneung city notices.

events.name: Yangyang Salmon Festival (Namdaecheon)
events.dates: Historically mid to late October; 2026 dates not verified
events.cost: Free entry; catch-a-salmon activities are paid

events.name: Seorak Cultural Festival
events.dates: Historically early to mid October (likely before Oct 17); 2026 dates not verified

tips: Do Seorak on a weekday. Mon Oct 19 to Fri Oct 23 is ideal, with peak color and far fewer jams than Sat/Sun.
For Seorak, buy cable car tickets first, then hike Biseondae while waiting for your assigned boarding time.
The best 'Kamakura' day is Naksansa at sunrise or morning, then Hajodae, Hyuhyuam and the Jukdo/Ingu surf cafés, ending at Sokcho's Jungang market.

The best 'onsen' substitutes nearby are Cheoksan Hot Spring (an outdoor bath in the pines, nude, single-sex) or Seorak Waterpia (outdoor hot-spring pools, swimsuit). Neither is a true ryokan. The Seongyojang hanok stay is the traditional-lodging pick.

Suggested 3-night east-coast loop: Seoul to Gangneung by KTX (2 h). Gangneung for one night (Gyeongpo, Ojukheon, Seongyojang, Anmok, Chodang). Bus to Sokcho or Yangyang for two nights (Naksansa, Seorak on a weekday, market). Then either bus back to Seoul, or return to Gangneung and take the KTX-Eum 09:36 down the coast to Gyeongju or Busan.
Odaesan fits as a stop between Seoul and Gangneung: get off the KTX at Jinbu, walk the fir path, and continue to Gangneung the same evening.

Transport for 3 people over this segment is roughly: KTX Seoul to Gangneung 27,600, bus Gangneung to Sokcho about 7,500, local buses and taxis about 30,000, and either bus Sokcho to Seoul about 25,000 or KTX-Eum Gangneung to Gyeongju 34,300. That is under about 100,000 KRW per person.
Admissions are cheap: Seorak, Naksansa and Woljeongsa are free since 2023. The cable car (16,000) is the main paid item, plus small fees at Ojukheon (3,000) and Seongyojang (5,000).
warnings: The Osaek cable car (Osaek to Kkeutcheong) is not open. It is still under construction as of July 2026, with no fixed opening date (projections run to about 2029) and rare-plant transplanting delayed. Do not plan on it.
There is no rail to Sokcho or Yangyang. The Chuncheon-Sokcho and Gangneung-Jejin lines are still under construction.

October weekend traffic around Seorak (Route 44 Hangyeryeong, Seorak-dong access road, Osaek) and on the Seoul-Yangyang expressway can add 1-3 hours. Avoid Sat/Sun for Seorak and for intercity travel, especially Sunday afternoon toward Seoul.
Gwongeumseong cable car waits on foliage weekends can exceed 1-2 hours, and only same-day tickets are sold on-site.
Heullimgol needs an advance KNPS reservation (5,000 people a day). Juongol from Osaek does not.

Lodging prices in this file are estimates from 2024-25 knowledge, because live booking sites could not be fetched. Late-October Saturdays are the year's peak for Sokcho and Seorak, so book immediately and expect 1.5-2x weekday rates.
